doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Enlisting in the Air Force: band to Panama, then junior college
summary: He enlisted alongside a friend and joined a band bound for Westover Field, but was sent to Panama. There he studied harmony and counterpoint, wrote a library and conducted a Caribbean tour, then went to junior college.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So 1946, did you decide to enlist? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

I did enlist, yes indeed I did. And what happened was I went to the Air Force, I was going to enlist in the Air Force. And the day we were being inducted there was a band, from San Diego, a young band. At this time Look Magazine had a band contest, nationwide. And this band placed third in the nationwide, from San Diego. And so they were inducted as a unit, they enlisted as a unit, and they were told that they would stay together and be stationed at Westover Field, Massachusetts, and play for recruiting purposes and entertainment, USO type things. The baritone player and the tenor player from that band didn’t pass the physical. And it happened to be that my friend, who was a baritone player, and is actually the reason I was enlisting because I was going to be drafted anyway so I thought we’d stay together. So we enlisted together and we joined that band, it was just a coincidence that it had worked out that way. Well they were not used for recruiting purposes, and my friend ended up in Newfoundland, and I went with the good part of this band to Panama.
That’s a long way from Massachusetts.

A long ways from Massachusetts. But that turned out to be a very good experience too because in Panama I started studying privately from a musician down there, studying harmony and counterpoint, and I wrote a library for that band as a young person, as I was, and we did a show that toured the Caribbean area: Haiti and Jamaica, Puerto Rico and a bunch of different places down there, for which I was the conductor of this band, and had written most of the music. So I thought that was going to be a start of something for me. And then when I got out of the service I went to a junior college in Los Angeles. Actually I wanted to go to Eastman and I made application and there was a two year wait at that time, so I didn’t want to wait so I got started. And I started studying harmony yet a third time from the very beginning, so it was easy for me.
